svg.title: Microsoft Fabric: Direct Lake Internals (Metadata, Framing & Fallback)
svg.desc: An internals infographic tracing how Direct Lake queries resolve between VertiPaq in-memory caching and OneLake storage: metadata framing lifecycle (v1 to v3), lazy column transcoding, V-Order optimization, and the DirectQuery fallback decision tree with SQL analytics endpoint integration.
svg.text: MICROSOFT FABRIC: DIRECT LAKE INTERNALS (METADATA, FRAMING & FALLBACK)

g.title: Query hits a residency state — A Direct Lake model sits in one of four memory-residency states, with latency improving at each step.
Cold query: transcoding — Direct Lake merges per-row-group local Parquet dictionaries into a single global VertiPaq dictionary.
Framing — A metadata-only refresh that rebinds the model to the current Delta commit's file set.
Which Direct Lake flavor? — DirectQuery fallback exists only in Direct Lake on SQL; Direct Lake on OneLake never falls back.
DirectQuery fallback (SQL flavor only) — Three documented triggers force a query to bypass Direct Lake and read the SQL endpoint directly.
g.text: Returns data live, but pays DAX-to-SQL lag
Files A, B, C, D, E

g.title: Row-group-to-segment mapping — Row groups map one-to-one to VertiPaq segments; sizing them right is the real performance lever.

g.text: • Direct Lake does not use min/max stats

g.title: Eviction triggers — Refresh, non-use, or memory pressure can evict a resident column back to cold.
g.text: 1. Framing Rebind: Source table modified ➔ evicts segments tied to removed row groups.
2. Prolonged Inactivity: Cold LRU eviction cleans unqueried column segments.
3. Capacity Memory Pressure: Concurrent queries/ETL force eviction capacity-wide.

g.title: Trap: Overwrite defeats incremental framing — Loading with Overwrite wipes commit history, forcing a full cold reload on the next query.
g.text: Trap: Overwrite Wipes Delta Commit History
• Loading Delta tables with mode("overwrite") destroys historical Delta commits.
• Defeats incremental framing; forces a 100% full cold reload of all segments & dictionaries.
• Remedy: Always use MERGE or append writes for Direct Lake-backed tables.

g.aria-label: Trap: SQL view silently forces fallback
g.title: Trap: SQL view silently forces fallback — A model table based on a SQL view forces every query into DirectQuery fallback.
g.text: Trap: SQL View Silently Forces DirectQuery Fallback
• Basing Direct Lake on SQL models on SQL views permanently triggers fallback on every query.
• The model still advertises Direct Lake mode, making the performance regression invisible.
• Remedy: Bind Direct Lake models directly to physical Delta base tables in OneLake.

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — Original Infographic, August 2026. Sourced from Microsoft Fabric Direct Lake Architecture & VertiPaq Engine Internals.
